```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Colin, Manolis and Koomen (2026) pooled the individual participant data of
the paediatric type 2 diabetes trials that supported EU extensions of
indication for seven antihyperglycaemic drugs, and fitted a longitudinal
disease-progression model of HbA1c in the tradition of Holford: a baseline
`S0`, a linear progression `S0 * alpha * t`, and a symptomatic response that
reaches a fraction `expit(theta + dTRT)` of baseline with a half-life of
onset. Placebo has `dTRT = 0`; each drug has its own placebo-corrected shift
`dTRT` on the logit scale. The model was then used for clinical trial
simulations of sample size.

```{r load-model}
mod <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Colin_2026_pediatricT2DM_hba1c_mbma")))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70468> (open access; the supplement
  holds the NONMEM control stream and final estimates as Text S1)

Loading the model prints an rxode2 note that `etalslope` and
`eta_study_lslope` are not mu-referenced. That is expected: the two etas
enter the progression rate through a Box-Cox transform, which cannot be
written as `lslope + eta`.

# Population

Seven products had individual patient listings in the EMA database (Table S1):
the DPP-4 inhibitors linagliptin, alogliptin, sitagliptin and saxagliptin,
the SGLT2 inhibitors empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, and the GLP-1 receptor
agonist exenatide (once weekly). Linagliptin and empagliflozin shared one
trial, so the data come from six studies. In all, 809 participants (456 on
active treatment) contributed 3295 HbA1c observations; the final model
excludes seven influential participants. Participants had a mean (SD) age of
14.6 (2.16) years, weight of 90.0 (27.2) kg and BMI-for-age z-score of 2.85
(1.27); 62% were female; the median time since diagnosis was 2.2 years (IQR
1.0-3.7). Background therapy was metformin (41%), metformin and insulin
(31%), insulin (10%) or none (18%). Per-study characteristics are in Table 1.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Source trace

All values are the final NONMEM estimates printed in Text S1 of the
supplement; Table 2 reports the same estimates back-transformed and rounded.

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lrbase` | 2.01 (7.46 %) | Text S1 TH1; Table 2 beta0 |
| `e_conmed_insulin_rbase` | 0.108 (1.11-fold) | Text S1 TH6; Table 2 beta1 |
| `e_t_diag_diab_rbase` | 0.0121 (1.012-fold per year) | Text S1 TH8; Table 2 beta2 |
| `lslope` | -2.05 (0.129 per year) | Text S1 TH2; Table 2 beta3 |
| `e_conmed_insulin_slope` | 0.545 (1.72-fold) | Text S1 TH7; Table 2 beta4 |
| `boxcox_lslope` | -0.315 | Text S1 TH16; Table 2 beta6 |
| `logitpbo` | -2.61 (0.07) | Text S1 TH3; Table 2 theta |
| `lthalf_onset` | 3.87 (47.9 day = 6.85 weeks) | Text S1 TH4; Table 2 beta5 |
| `e_trt_linagliptin_logitpbo` | 0.265 | Text S1 TH9; Table 2 dTRT,1 |
| `e_trt_empagliflozin_logitpbo` | 1.03 | Text S1 TH10; Table 2 dTRT,2 |
| `e_trt_alogliptin_logitpbo` | 0.532 | Text S1 TH11; Table 2 dTRT,3 |
| `e_trt_exenatide_logitpbo` | 1.28 | Text S1 TH12; Table 2 dTRT,4 |
| `e_trt_sitagliptin_logitpbo` | 0.377 | Text S1 TH13; Table 2 dTRT,5 |
| `e_trt_saxagliptin_logitpbo` | 0.971 | Text S1 TH14; Table 2 dTRT,6 |
| `e_trt_dapagliflozin_logitpbo` | 0.954 | Text S1 TH15; Table 2 dTRT,7 |
| `etalrbase`, `etalslope`, `etalogitpbo` block | 0.0212; 0.0277, 4.18; 0.0333, 1.69, 1.91 | Text S1 OMEGA, ETA1-ETA3 |
| `eta_study_lrbase`, `eta_study_lslope` block | 4.77e-4; 1.85e-3, 0.0120 | Text S1 OMEGA, ETA4-ETA5 |
| `expSd` | sqrt(3.42e-3) = 0.0585 | Text S1 SIGMA |
| Baseline `S0` | `exp(lrbase + eta) * exp(0.108 * INS) * exp(0.0121 * (DIA - 2.5))` | Eq. 3; Text S1 `S0` |
| Progression rate with Box-Cox eta | `exp(lslope + ((exp(eta))^lambda - 1) / lambda) * exp(0.545 * INS)` | Eqs. 4-5; Text S1 `ALPHA`, `ETA_ALPHA` |
| Symptomatic response | `S0 * expit(theta + eta + dTRT) * (1 - exp(-log(2) / t1/2 * t))` | Eq. 6; Text S1 `PLACBO`, `DRUG` |
| HbA1c | `S0 * (1 + alpha * t / 365) - response` | Eq. 1; Text S1 `IPLAC`, `IDRUG` |
| Residual error | `log(HbA1c) + eps` | Methods; Text S1 `Y = LOG(IPRED) + ERR(1)` |

The control stream codes treatment as one categorical column `TRT` = 0-7.
The model uses one indicator per drug, `TRT_LINAGLIPTIN` = `TRT` 1 through
`TRT_DAPAGLIFLOZIN` = `TRT` 7; how that order was established is explained
under Assumptions and deviations.

# Simulation set-up

The random effects for every check below are drawn in R from the model's own
OMEGA block with a fixed seed and passed to `rxSolve()` as per-subject
parameters, together with the fixed effects. This has two benefits: each
virtual participant is solved under placebo and under active treatment with
the *same* random effects, so the placebo-corrected effect is estimated
without between-arm sampling noise; and the cohort is identical on every
machine, because rxode2 draws no random numbers. Residual error is likewise
added in R where it is needed.

The paper's trial simulations included between-subject and within-subject
variability only, so the between-study etas are set to zero here.

```{r helpers}
trt_cols <- c(
  "TRT_LINAGLIPTIN", "TRT_EMPAGLIFLOZIN", "TRT_ALOGLIPTIN", "TRT_EXENATIDE",
  "TRT_SITAGLIPTIN", "TRT_SAXAGLIPTIN", "TRT_DAPAGLIFLOZIN"
)
drug_names <- c(
  "Linagliptin", "Empagliflozin", "Alogliptin", "Exenatide",
  "Sitagliptin", "Saxagliptin", "Dapagliflozin"
)
eta_subj <- c("etalrbase", "etalslope", "etalogitpbo")
omega_subj <- mod$omega[eta_subj, eta_subj]
theta <- mod$theta
sd_resid <- unname(theta["expSd"])

# One virtual cohort. `dur_meanlog` / `dur_sdlog` give a log-normal diabetes
# duration; a duration of 0 codes 'missing', which the model replaces by the
# 2.5-year reference.
make_subjects <- function(n, seed, p_insulin, dur_meanlog, dur_sdlog,
                          p_dur_missing = 0) {
  set.seed(seed)
  eta <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n) %*% chol(omega_subj)
  colnames(eta) <- eta_subj
  dur <- exp(rnorm(n, dur_meanlog, dur_sdlog))
  dur[runif(n) < p_dur_missing] <- 0
  data.frame(
    id = seq_len(n),
    CONMED_INSULIN = as.integer(runif(n) < p_insulin),
    T_DIAG_DIAB = dur,
    eta,
    eta_study_lrbase = 0,
    eta_study_lslope = 0
  )
}

# Solve one arm. `drug` is a TRT_ column (NULL = placebo); `dtrt` optionally
# replaces that drug's estimated logit shift with a scenario value.
solve_arm <- function(subj, times, drug = NULL, dtrt = NULL) {
  ev <- tidyr::crossing(
    subj[, c("id", "CONMED_INSULIN", "T_DIAG_DIAB")],
    time = times
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  for (v in trt_cols) ev[[v]] <- 0L
  th <- theta
  if (!is.null(drug)) {
    ev[[drug]] <- 1L
    if (!is.null(dtrt)) th[[paste0("e_", tolower(drug), "_logitpbo")]] <- dtrt
  }
  params <- cbind(
    subj[, c("id", eta_subj, "eta_study_lrbase", "eta_study_lslope")],
    as.data.frame(as.list(th))
  )
  # rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega; the etas are
  # supplied explicitly in `params`, which is the intent.
  sim <- suppressWarnings(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = params, returnType = "data.frame")
  )
  # A single-subject solve returns no id column.
  if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- subj$id[1]
  sim[, c("id", "time", "Hba1c")]
}

# Change from baseline per subject between the first and last time.
change_from_baseline <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(cfb = Hba1c[which.max(time)] - Hba1c[which.min(time)], .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::pull(cfb)
}
```

# Typical-value checks

These are deterministic: a typical participant (all etas zero) without
insulin and with a 2.5-year history, unless stated otherwise.

```{r typical}
typical <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4, etalrbase = 0, etalslope = 0, etalogitpbo = 0,
  eta_study_lrbase = 0, eta_study_lslope = 0
)
typ_subj <- function(ins) {
  dplyr::mutate(typical[1, ], CONMED_INSULIN = ins, T_DIAG_DIAB = 2.5)
}
expit <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

s0_noins <- solve_arm(typ_subj(0), 0)$Hba1c
s0_ins <- solve_arm(typ_subj(1), 0)$Hba1c

# Placebo and drug at a time long enough for the response to be complete
# (50 half-lives of onset). Progression cancels in the drug-minus-placebo
# difference, which is the paper's Eq. 7.
t_long <- 50 * exp(theta[["lthalf_onset"]])
pbo_long <- solve_arm(typ_subj(0), t_long)$Hba1c
eq7 <- vapply(trt_cols, function(d) {
  solve_arm(typ_subj(0), t_long, d)$Hba1c - pbo_long
}, numeric(1))
pct_decrease <- 100 * expit(theta[["logitpbo"]] + theta[paste0("e_", tolower(trt_cols), "_logitpbo")])

# Change from baseline at 26 weeks for a hypothetical dTRT = 0.85.
cfb26 <- function(ins) {
  s <- solve_arm(typ_subj(ins), c(0, 26 * 7), "TRT_LINAGLIPTIN", dtrt = 0.85)
  diff(s$Hba1c)
}

# 95% prediction interval of the yearly fold-increase for a participant not
# on insulin (Box-Cox eta on the progression rate).
lam <- theta[["boxcox_lslope"]]
sd_slope <- sqrt(mod$omega["etalslope", "etalslope"])
alpha_at <- function(z) {
  eta <- z * sd_slope
  exp(theta[["lslope"]] + (exp(lam * eta) - 1) / lam)
}
alpha_pi <- 1 + alpha_at(c(-1.96, 1.96))

# 95% prediction interval of the placebo response at a 7.46% baseline.
sd_pbo <- sqrt(mod$omega["etalogitpbo", "etalogitpbo"])
pbo_pi <- -7.46 * expit(theta[["logitpbo"]] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * sd_pbo)

typ_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Paper, ~Model,
  "Baseline HbA1c, no insulin (%)", 7.46, s0_noins,
  "Baseline HbA1c, insulin (%)", 8.31, s0_ins,
  "Placebo response at 7.46% baseline (%-points)", -0.52, pbo_long - s0_noins - s0_noins * alpha_at(0) * t_long / 365,
  "Expected decrease from baseline, linagliptin (%)", 9, pct_decrease[[1]],
  "Expected decrease from baseline, exenatide (%)", 21, pct_decrease[[4]],
  "Eq. 7 dHbA1c, linagliptin (%-points)", -0.14, eq7[["TRT_LINAGLIPTIN"]],
  "Eq. 7 dHbA1c, exenatide (%-points)", -1.05, eq7[["TRT_EXENATIDE"]],
  "26-week change, dTRT 0.85, no insulin (%-points)", -0.53, cfb26(0),
  "26-week change, dTRT 0.85, insulin (%-points)", -0.21, cfb26(1),
  "Yearly fold-increase, upper 95% limit", 2.25, alpha_pi[2],
  "Placebo response 95% PI, largest decrease (%-points)", -3.91, pbo_pi[2]
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = signif(Model, 3), `Difference (%)` = round(100 * (Model - Paper) / abs(Paper), 1))
knitr::kable(typ_tab, caption = "Typical-value quantities quoted in the Results text.")

stopifnot(
  # Every quoted value is a back-transform of the final estimates, so the
  # model reproduces each to within the paper's rounding.
  all(abs(typ_tab$Model - typ_tab$Paper) <= pmax(0.02, 0.025 * abs(typ_tab$Paper)) | grepl("decrease from baseline", typ_tab$Quantity)),
  all(abs(typ_tab$Model - typ_tab$Paper)[grepl("decrease from baseline", typ_tab$Quantity)] < 0.6),
  # The paper's 95% PI for the yearly fold-increase starts at 1-fold.
  abs(alpha_pi[1] - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The placebo response is 0.511 %-points with the unrounded estimate
`expit(-2.61)` = 0.0685; the paper's 0.52 multiplies 7.46 by the rounded 0.07.

The other end of the paper's placebo prediction interval is quoted as
"-0.3 %-points"; the final estimates give
`r signif(pbo_pi[1], 2)` %-points (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Placebo-corrected effect and its variability (Table 3)

The paper's trial simulations resampled participants from the pooled data,
randomised them 1:1 and simulated 26 weeks. Table 3 lists, for each scenario
value of `dTRT`, the corresponding mean placebo-corrected change from
baseline (dHbA1c). The cohort below approximates the pooled population: 41%
on insulin (insulin alone 10% plus metformin and insulin 31%), a log-normal
diabetes duration with the reported median of 2.2 years and IQR of 1.0-3.7
years, and the duration missing (so set to the 2.5-year reference) for 32% of
participants, the share of the pooled data from the sitagliptin and
dapagliflozin studies, which did not record it (Table 1).

```{r table3}
n_cts <- 200
cts_subj <- make_subjects(
  n_cts,
  seed = 2026, p_insulin = 0.41,
  dur_meanlog = log(2.2), dur_sdlog = log(3.7 / 1.0) / (2 * qnorm(0.75)),
  p_dur_missing = 0.32
)
wk26 <- c(0, 26 * 7)
pbo26 <- solve_arm(cts_subj, wk26)
cfb_pbo <- change_from_baseline(pbo26)

table3 <- tibble::tibble(
  dTRT = c(0.40, 0.52, 0.64, 0.74, 0.85, 0.95, 1.04, 1.14),
  paper = c(-0.30, -0.40, -0.50, -0.60, -0.70, -0.80, -0.90, -1.00)
)
table3$model <- vapply(table3$dTRT, function(d) {
  mean(change_from_baseline(solve_arm(cts_subj, wk26, "TRT_LINAGLIPTIN", dtrt = d)) - cfb_pbo)
}, numeric(1))

table3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "dTRT (logit)" = dTRT,
    "dHbA1c, Table 3 (%-points)" = paper,
    "dHbA1c, model (%-points)" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean placebo-corrected change from baseline at 26 weeks (Table 3).")

stopifnot(
  # A transcription error in theta, the onset half-life, the time unit or
  # the logit structure moves these by tens of percent.
  abs(median(table3$model - table3$paper)) < 0.05,
  all(abs(table3$model - table3$paper) < 0.10)
)
```

The paper also reports the spread of the change from baseline in the placebo
arm: a median SD of 1.83 %-points across virtual trials (95% prediction
interval 1.15-2.49), and 1.30 (0.97-1.62) in an enriched population of
participants not on insulin with less than 2.2 years of diabetes.

```{r placebo-sd}
set.seed(26)
pbo_obs <- pbo26 |>
  dplyr::mutate(obs = Hba1c * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_resid)))
cfb_obs <- change_from_baseline(dplyr::mutate(pbo_obs, Hba1c = obs))

enrich_subj <- make_subjects(
  n_cts,
  seed = 2027, p_insulin = 0,
  dur_meanlog = log(1.0), dur_sdlog = 0.5
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(T_DIAG_DIAB = pmin(T_DIAG_DIAB, 2.19))
set.seed(27)
enrich_obs <- solve_arm(enrich_subj, wk26) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Hba1c = Hba1c * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_resid)))
cfb_enrich <- change_from_baseline(enrich_obs)

sd_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Population, ~`Paper median SD`, ~`Paper 95% PI`, ~`Model SD`,
  "Historical trial population", 1.83, "1.15-2.49", sd(cfb_obs),
  "Enriched (no insulin, < 2.2 years)", 1.30, "0.97-1.62", sd(cfb_enrich)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Model SD` = round(`Model SD`, 2))
knitr::kable(sd_tab, caption = "SD of the 26-week change from baseline in the placebo arm (%-points).")

stopifnot(
  sd(cfb_obs) > 1.15, sd(cfb_obs) < 2.49,
  sd(cfb_enrich) > 0.97, sd(cfb_enrich) < 1.62,
  sd(cfb_enrich) < sd(cfb_obs)
)
```

The enriched cohort draws durations from a log-normal centred on 1 year and
capped just below 2.2 years; the paper resampled the actual participants
meeting the criteria, whose duration distribution is not reported.

# Placebo-corrected effect by drug (Figure 2)

Figure 2 compares the observed dHbA1c of each trial with the median model
prediction (black diamonds). The model predictions below use one virtual
cohort per drug whose insulin use and diabetes duration follow that study's
row of Table 1, solved at the time of the trial's primary endpoint (Table
S1). Duration is set to the 2.5-year reference for the sitagliptin and
dapagliflozin studies, which did not record it. The published medians were
digitised by the maintainers from Figure 2.

```{r figure2}
studies <- tibble::tibble(
  drug = trt_cols,
  name = drug_names,
  # Insulin alone + metformin and insulin, Table 1 (%).
  p_insulin = c(3.2 + 40, 3.2 + 40, 5.3 + 35, 7.4 + 41, 18 + 10, 12 + 37, 17 + 29) / 100,
  dur_mean = c(2.10, 2.10, 3.38, 2.31, NA, 2.48, NA),
  dur_sd = c(1.90, 1.90, 1.84, 2.12, NA, 2.14, NA),
  weeks = c(26, 26, 26, 24, 20, 26, 24),
  fig2_median = c(-0.25, -0.78, -0.32, -1.05, -0.25, -0.84, -0.72)
)

fig2 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(studies)), function(i) {
  st <- studies[i, ]
  if (is.na(st$dur_mean)) {
    meanlog <- log(2.5)
    sdlog <- 0
    p_miss <- 1
  } else {
    sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (st$dur_sd / st$dur_mean)^2))
    meanlog <- log(st$dur_mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
    p_miss <- 0
  }
  subj <- make_subjects(n_cts, seed = 3000 + i, p_insulin = st$p_insulin,
                        dur_meanlog = meanlog, dur_sdlog = sdlog,
                        p_dur_missing = p_miss)
  tt <- c(0, st$weeks * 7)
  d <- change_from_baseline(solve_arm(subj, tt, st$drug)) -
    change_from_baseline(solve_arm(subj, tt))
  tibble::tibble(name = st$name, model = mean(d), paper = st$fig2_median)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

fig2 |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Drug" = name,
    "Model dHbA1c (%-points)" = model,
    "Figure 2 median prediction (%-points)" = paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Placebo-corrected change from baseline at each trial's primary endpoint.")

fig2 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(model, paper), names_to = "source", values_to = "dhba1c") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = dplyr::recode(source, model = "This model", paper = "Figure 2 (digitised)"),
    name = factor(name, levels = rev(c("Alogliptin", "Sitagliptin", "Linagliptin", "Saxagliptin",
                                       "Exenatide", "Empagliflozin", "Dapagliflozin")))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(dhba1c, name, shape = source, colour = source)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "dHbA1c (%-points)", y = NULL, shape = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the median predictions of Figure 2 of Colin 2026.") +
  theme_bw()

stopifnot(
  # Approximate per-study covariates and digitisation limit the agreement;
  # a mis-assigned drug effect would be off by 0.3-0.9 %-points.
  median(abs(fig2$model - fig2$paper)) < 0.10,
  all(abs(fig2$model - fig2$paper) < 0.20)
)
```

# HbA1c over time by arm (Figure 1)

Figure 1 is a prediction-corrected visual predictive check by arm. Without
the trial data the figure below shows the model's 5th, 50th and 95th
percentiles of HbA1c (with residual error) for each arm of the virtual
population, which can be compared with the bands of Figure 1: a placebo
median near 7.5% with 5th and 95th percentiles near 5.5-6% and 10-11%, and
the active arms drifting down from a similar baseline.

```{r figure1}
grid <- seq(0, 26 * 7, by = 7)
arms <- c(list(Placebo = NULL), setNames(as.list(trt_cols), drug_names))
vpc <- lapply(names(arms), function(a) {
  set.seed(match(a, names(arms)))
  solve_arm(cts_subj, grid, arms[[a]]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = a, Hba1c = Hba1c * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_resid)))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Hba1c, 0.05), p50 = median(Hba1c), p95 = quantile(Hba1c, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = names(arms)))

ggplot(vpc, aes(time / 7)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~arm, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "HbA1c (%)",
       caption = "Compare with Figure 1 of Colin 2026 (same percentiles, simulated cohort of 200 per arm).") +
  theme_bw()

pbo_wk21 <- dplyr::filter(vpc, arm == "Placebo", time == 21 * 7)
stopifnot(
  pbo_wk21$p50 > 7.0, pbo_wk21$p50 < 8.0,
  pbo_wk21$p95 > 9.5, pbo_wk21$p95 < 12,
  pbo_wk21$p05 > 4.5, pbo_wk21$p05 < 6.5
)
```

# NCA

Not applicable: the model describes HbA1c, not a drug concentration, and has
no dose events. The checks above take the place of an NCA comparison.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Drug order of the treatment effects.** Table 2 and the control stream
  label the drug effects only as TRT 1-7. The order linagliptin,
  empagliflozin, alogliptin, exenatide, sitagliptin, saxagliptin,
  dapagliflozin is the order of Table S1 and of the panels of Figure 1, and
  it is consistent with every statement in the Results: linagliptin has the
  smallest effect (9%, TRT 1 = 0.26) and exenatide the largest (21%, TRT 4 =
  1.28); the 95% CIs that include zero (TRT 1, 3 and 5) belong to linagliptin,
  alogliptin and sitagliptin; and the control stream marks TRT 2, 4 and 7 as
  'approved', matching the three drugs with an EU paediatric indication
  (empagliflozin, exenatide, dapagliflozin). The Table 3 and Figure 2 checks
  above confirm the assignment.
* **Response scaled by baseline.** Equations 1 and 6 print the symptomatic
  response as a fraction subtracted from HbA1c; the control stream multiplies
  it by `S0` (`DOSEP = -S0*PBO`, `DRUG = -S0*...`), as does Equation 7. The
  model follows the control stream.
* **Between-study SD of the progression rate.** Table 2 prints omega5 = 0.35
  (0.30; 0.39); the variance in the NONMEM output is 0.0120 (SD 0.110, as in
  the printed correlation matrix). The model uses the NONMEM output, which is
  what was fitted.
* **Placebo prediction interval.** The Results quote a 95% prediction
  interval for the placebo response of -0.3 to -3.91 %-points at a 7.46%
  baseline. The upper end is reproduced; the final estimates give
  `r signif(pbo_pi[1], 2)` %-points for the lower end.
* **Missing diabetes duration.** The Methods state that missing covariates
  were imputed by the median (2.2 years); the control stream sets the
  duration to the 2.5-year reference whenever `DIAGNOSIS` is not positive.
  The model follows the control stream: code a missing duration as 0.
* **Box-Cox transform.** As in the control stream, the transform is applied
  to the sum of the subject and study etas on the progression rate.
* **Nested between-study variability.** rxode2 has no study level, so
  `eta_study_lrbase` and `eta_study_lslope` are drawn per subject by
  default. To simulate trials, give every subject of a study the same values
  (as `params`), or set them to zero as here. Between-study variability was
  under 20% of the between-subject variability.
* **Unused parameter.** THETA5 of the control stream ('NOT USED', fixed to 6)
  does not enter any equation and is omitted.
* **Times before randomisation.** HbA1c records before time 0 are evaluated
  at time 0 (no progression or response), as in the control stream.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Covariate distributions are approximations built from
  the summary statistics of Table 1 and the Results; the trial data are not
  public. The paper's trial simulations resampled the pooled participants.
